## What does this mean?

Which request types, evidence gaps, and operational constraints make a ranking or reference method unreliable?

## Why does it matter?

An approach may work overall yet fail on ambiguous names, time-sensitive facts,
or queries unlike its training neighborhood. We want a warning signal before
trusting it.

## How does it work?

<ol class="hub-process hub-record-path">
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Question</strong><br>When do promising signals fail?</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Evidence</strong><br>7 studies addresses this question.</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Bounded answer</strong><br>Failures cluster around ambiguity, entity resolution, evidence custody, scope changes, and over-tuned fusion, but no complete predictor exists.</li>

## What do we know?

Failures cluster around ambiguity, entity resolution, evidence custody, scope changes, and over-tuned fusion, but no complete predictor exists.

**Confidence:** Low

## What is missing?

Observed development and audit failures are diagnostic; they do not estimate hidden-test prevalence.

Known failures are selected observations, not an unbiased error-rate estimate.
Restricted pilots and invalid systems remain outside full-development
comparisons.

**Open subquestions**

- Can failure clusters be detected before a decision?
- Can reliability-aware fusion improve without adding leakage?
